findings.evidence: The text reads, in the present tense: 'Automated as `.claude/scripts/tests/workflow-manifest.test.sh` Section 6, which runs this comparison on every L1 run for whichever release `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` currently names, and prints a `note:` skip rather than a failure when that tag or table is not in the checkout.' This change set DELETED Section 6 (verified: the '--- SECTION 6: REMOVED (claude-workflow-plugin-h2zz waiver ruling, round 4)' tombstone now stands in its place, and grep confirms no Section 6 remains). All three clauses are now false: the section does not exist, the comparison does not run on every L1 run, and no `note:` skip is printed. HANDOFF.md self-describes at line 3 as 'the cross-session handoff record. Read it first when picking up work on this repository', and it carries an explicit supersession convention used elsewhere ('[SUPERSEDED by the bullet above ... Kept unedited as the record of what was true when d2j.1 landed.]') plus dated live-check markers as recent as 2026-09-19 - so it is actively maintained and this line carries no staleness marker of any kind.
findings.description: The change set relocated the tag/table reproducibility claim and left the repo's primary read-first document pointing at the deleted mechanism. Every IN-FILE pointer got a tombstone (run-tests.sh, runner-completeness.test.sh, workflow-manifest.test.sh, test.yml) - the sweep was file-scoped, never repo-scoped, so the one pointer outside the changed files survived. Consequence for a real releaser: HANDOFF.md tells them the check is automatic on every L1 run, so they never learn to run `make verify-release`, and the pre-push half of the two-context design documented in verify-release-manifest.sh's own header ('(a) LOCALLY ... run as part of a release checklist') is wired into no checklist that exists - grep finds zero references to verify-release in any .md in the repo. Not HIGH because release-verify.yml still enforces the claim post-push by construction, so no bad release escapes undetected; it is caught after the tag is pushed rather than before. FIX: update HANDOFF.md:694-698 to name .claude/scripts/verify-release-manifest.sh / `make verify-release` / release-verify.yml, matching the tombstone wording used everywhere else in this change set. Worth doing in the same pass: HANDOFF.md:457-462 records v5.0.0 byte-reproducibility as an OPEN gap ('What this does NOT assert: that the table is byte-reproducible from a tagged v5.0.0 checkout'), which this change set's own tooling now answers - measured this review: `make verify-release` -> OK, 138 rows, rc=0.

findings.evidence: grep across .claude/scripts/tests/ and .claude/tests/ finds NO assertion referencing release-verify.yml - every hit is a prose mention inside a comment (workflow-manifest.test.sh:47,87; verify-release-manifest.test.sh:279; run-tests.sh:1412). The file parses as valid YAML (checked: trigger 'push', one job) but nothing in the suite asserts that it exists, that it triggers on tags 'v*', that it retains 'fetch-depth: 0', or that RELEASE_TAG is passed via 'env:' rather than interpolated into the run: script. That last one is the R5-F5 SECURITY fix in this very file; its Makefile twin (R6-F2, the identical injection class) received 15 assertions including a mutant that genuinely executes the injected command and proves it masks the real exit 2. The YAML twin received zero.
findings.description: release-verify.yml is one of the two named PRODUCTION contexts for the relocated claim and is the only one that is automatic, yet it ships with no coverage at all. This is a direct violation of the repo's own rule in CLAUDE.md: 'if you are adding a new CHECK of any kind (assertion, guard, CI job, gate condition) -> ... it does not ship without a negative control, and at least one leg must observe the shipped artifact RUNNING.' A new CI job is named explicitly there. Direct precedent exists in this repo for exactly this shape: workflow-doctor.test.sh:1489-1520 asserts on .github/workflows/windows-install.yml - a workflow that runs just as rarely - including the NEGATIVE assertion 'the check count is NOT compared against a hardcoded literal' pinning the precise anti-pattern its fix closed. The risk is not hypothetical: the workflow cannot be exercised before a real 'v*' tag push, so any regression surfaces only on release day, at the one moment it is needed; and this same change set REMOVED 'fetch-depth: 0' from the l1-unit job, so a later consistency cleanup removing it from release-verify.yml too would silently break `git archive <tag>` with nothing to catch it. FIX: add a short section to verify-release-manifest.test.sh mirroring the windows-install.yml precedent - the workflow exists; it triggers on tags 'v*'; it sets fetch-depth: 0; RELEASE_TAG is bound under 'env:'; and the NEGATIVE leg, that '${{ github.ref_name }}' does NOT appear inside the run: block.

findings.description: Ten rounds of genuine dual-family review happened and left no durable record on the task - only files on disk that nothing points at. `qa-gate.sh approve` would have refused on this alone, and a future reader auditing whether the approval-cites-independent-review invariant held would find nothing. Recording THIS artifact repairs the gate predicate going forward but does not backfill the history. Recommend the orchestrator backfill r5/r6/r7/r8/r10 via `qa-gate.sh review-record <tid> --file docs/reviews/claude-workflow-plugin-h2zz-r<n>.json` (each already sits at the canonical derived path), so the ten-round dual-family trail this task is rightly proud of actually survives. Deliberately NOT backfilled by me: authoring another reviewer's records on their behalf is not mine to do unannounced. Related and separately low: the only COMPLETION v1 payload on disk is round 9's (4 files), while the change set carries 13 reviewable source paths - the specialist flagged this staleness itself in a task comment rather than hiding it, and approve's completeness cross-check is warn-only, so it does not block.
